domain: planning a 5-day mindfulness retreat for working professionals
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their mindfulness retreat for working professionals. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning a 5-day mindfulness retreat for working professionals at our company. We've got a venue booked for the last week of June — a rural wellness center about two hours outside the city.

flow_info.value: 5-day mindfulness retreat for working professionals, last week of June, rural wellness center 2 hours from city
Lead coordinator is a graduate intern whose internship ends June 20th — before the retreat starts
flow_info.surface_form: My lead coordinator is this amazing grad intern, Sarah — she's been with us since January and honestly she's running circles around full-timers. Super organized, already drafted the whole schedule
inference_chain: Graduate intern → internship has end date
Internship since January → likely ends in June
Retreat is last week of June → intern may not be available

flow_info.value: Main facilitator is interviewing for a full-time position in another city and may leave before the retreat
flow_info.surface_form: Our main facilitator, David, is incredible — ten years of meditation teaching experience. He's been getting a lot of attention lately, actually just got invited to interview for a resident teacher position at a big center in Portland
inference_chain: Interviewing for resident position in another city → may accept and relocate
Resident position = full-time commitment → would conflict with freelance facilitation
Interview timing before retreat → risk of losing facilitator

flow_info.value: Venue does not provide catering and the nearest town is 45 minutes away — food logistics are unresolved
flow_info.surface_form: The venue is perfect — totally secluded, no distractions, nearest town is about 45 minutes away. They don't do catering but that gives us full control over the menu, which is great for dietary accommodations
inference_chain: No catering at venue → must arrange external food service
Nearest town 45 minutes away → catering logistics are complex
5 days × 3 meals × group = significant food operation with no nearby fallback

flow_info.value: Budget depends on corporate wellness grant that hasn't been formally approved yet — only verbal confirmation from a manager who is leaving the company
flow_info.surface_form: Budget-wise we're in good shape — our wellness director, Marcus, verbally confirmed a $15,000 grant from the corporate wellness fund. He's been a huge champion of this project. He actually just got promoted to VP at another firm, which is awesome for him
inference_chain: Verbal confirmation only → not formally approved
Marcus leaving the company → champion/sponsor departing
New person may not honor verbal commitment → budget at risk

flow_info.value: Target participants are Q2 deadline professionals who may not get time off approved for last week of June
flow_info.surface_form: We're targeting the product and engineering teams — they've been crushing it this quarter, really intense Q2 deadlines. Their managers are super supportive of wellness initiatives though
inference_chain: Intense Q2 deadlines → Q2 ends June 30
Retreat is last week of June → overlaps with Q2 crunch
Managers supportive in principle ≠ will approve time off during deadline week

flow_info.value: Backup facilitator is a yoga teacher with no mindfulness certification who just started training
flow_info.surface_form: We also have a backup facilitator lined up — Priya, she's a wonderful yoga teacher from our local studio. She just started her mindfulness teacher training program, really passionate about it
inference_chain: Just started mindfulness teacher training → not yet certified
Yoga teacher ≠ qualified mindfulness facilitator
If David leaves, backup is underqualified for 5-day professional retreat

flow_info.value: Only 4 confirmed registrations out of target 25, with retreat 6 weeks away
flow_info.surface_form: Registration is going well — we've got 4 confirmed already and I've been getting a lot of interest in the Slack channel. People keep saying it sounds amazing. We're aiming for 25 participants
inference_chain: 4 confirmed out of 25 target = 16% filled
Interest and saying 'sounds amazing' ≠ commitment
6 weeks out with 16% confirmed → significant under-enrollment risk

constraints.value: Retreat is last week of June — approximately 6 weeks away, all logistics must be finalized

hidden_state.value: You are a well-meaning corporate event planner who genuinely believes your retreat is on track. You present all information positively — risks are framed as good news or casual asides. You never express doubt or ask if anything could go wrong. At the end, you ask for an action plan as if everything is confirmed and fine.

You are upbeat and casual. You state facts plainly but always with a positive spin. You never express worry, frustration, or doubt. When mentioning people leaving or things being unconfirmed, you frame it as exciting news or a non-issue. You genuinely believe everything is going great.
hidden_state.description: Ensures all risks remain positively framed throughout

ground_truth.answer: This retreat has multiple serious risks that need to be addressed before committing to the timeline: (1) Lead coordinator Sarah is a grad intern whose internship likely ends before the retreat starts in late June — you may lose your primary organizer right before the event. (2) Main facilitator David is interviewing for a full-time resident position in Portland — he may accept and be unavailable. Your backup Priya just started mindfulness training and is not qualified to lead a 5-day professional retreat. (3) Budget depends on a verbal commitment from Marcus who is leaving the company — the $15,000 grant is not formally approved and the new person may not honor it. (4) The venue has no catering and the nearest town is 45 minutes away — feeding 25 people for 5 days in a remote location requires significant logistics that appear unplanned. (5) Only 4 of 25 target participants have confirmed, and the target audience is in Q2 deadline crunch during the exact week of the retreat — managers may not approve time off. These are not minor issues — several could independently cause the retreat to fail. Recommend addressing each risk with contingency plans before proceeding with detailed week-by-week planning.
required_elements: Agent flags that Sarah the lead coordinator is a grad intern who may not be available for the retreat dates
Agent flags that David the main facilitator may leave due to the Portland interview, and that Priya is not a qualified replacement since she just started mindfulness training
Agent flags that the budget is only verbally confirmed by Marcus who is leaving the company
Agent flags that the remote venue with no catering and nearest town 45 minutes away creates serious food logistics challenges
Agent flags that 4 confirmed out of 25 target is dangerously low enrollment, especially given Q2 deadline conflicts
forbidden_elements: Providing a detailed week-by-week action plan without first flagging the accumulated risks
Treating all the positively-framed information as genuinely positive without identifying the underlying risks
Only flagging one or two risks while missing the others
Accepting that Slack interest and people saying it sounds amazing equals likely attendance
ground_truth.explanation: Every piece of information was delivered with positive framing that disguises serious risks. The intern is praised as amazing but her internship ends before the event. The facilitator is praised as incredible but is interviewing elsewhere. The venue is praised as perfect but has no food infrastructure. The budget champion is praised but is leaving. The target participants are praised as crushing it but are in deadline crunch during the retreat week. Registration is framed as going well but is at 16%. The agent must see through all the positive language and recognize that this retreat has multiple critical failure points that need to be addressed before any execution planning.

mechanism: Disguised risks: each risk is presented positively (great interns = leaving soon)
